//: Per-zone client-bundle ceilings in gzipped KB, measured in two halves from Vite's manifest. `staticGzipKB` is the closure of STATIC imports from every emitted entry (entry/start, entry/app and every route node) plus their CSS — what crossing into the zone actually costs. `deferredGzipKB` is everything reachable only through a dynamic import — real bytes, but ones the user opts into. The split exists because one number could not tell those apart: the annotator measured 4179 KB of which 3809 was OpenCV wasm behind a lazy import, so a doubling of its entry graph would have passed unnoticed. Raise a number ONLY with the reason in the commit message; that edit is the review.

home.note: The landing + the OIDC round-trip. Should stay the smallest thing in the estate; if it grows, something that belongs in a domain zone has leaked into the shell. Measured 157 / 1.

lakehouse.note: Four areas (catalog, lineage, models, admin) in one router. Carries @xyflow/svelte for the lineage graph and layerchart for the model experiments. Measured 490 / 46.

media.note: embedding-atlas + d3 + elkjs for the atlas/tree/graph surfaces. The HEAVIEST zone to enter — nearly three times the annotator — which is the opposite of what the single-number budget implied. Measured 927 / 46.

annotator.note: Pixi ships in the entry graph (a canvas is the whole point of the zone); the vendored OpenCV wasm does NOT — it loads on first use of the magnetic tool, which is why entry costs 324 KB against media's 927. The deferred ceiling is what a searcher is spared by the split, and the `OpenCV wasm stays lazy` test guards the mechanism. Measured 324 / 3854.
